2027 Suzuki GSX-10R Is All About the Brutal Engine Power of a True Sportsbike
25 photos
Photo: Suzuki
The GSX-R family of Suzuki sportsbikes will have a new member come the summer of next year. Shown for the first time in the metal at the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show that takes place this week in Milan, Italy, the newcomer seems, at least on paper, as unforgiving to the competition as it is brutal in terms of specs.
Drawing on the GSX-R1000R , the new two-wheeler is built around a new aluminum frame that comes complete with a new swingarm and a new subframe. Inside it there is a fresh interpretation of the K5 engine, the inline four-cylinder that in this application is rated at 150 horsepower at 11,000 rpm and 106 Nm of torque at 9,250 rpm.
The engine has been revised inside and out, as, according to the Japanese bike maker, it not only needs to fulfill the demands of today's riders, be them for the tracks or public roads, but it also needs to be future-proof against the introduction of upcoming alcohol-based fuels.
To that end, the heart of the machine comes with new cams, camshafts, cam chain sprocket, cylinder head, barrels, and cases. The new setup ties into a four-into-one exhaust and a transmission controlled through Suzuki's Slipper Clutch Assist system.
The new motorcycle has been propped on cast aluminum wheels sized 17 inches on both ends, shod in Bridgestone Battlax Hypersport S23 tires. Brembo braking hardware is connected to both of them, with the front one also tied to fully adjustable 43 mm KYB forks and the one at the opposite end to a shock specifically designed for it.
The bike's operation is governed by an electronics package that bundles together a six-axis IMU with slide, roll torque, traction, and wheelie control, among others. When it comes to riding position, the new bike copies a lot from the GSX-R1000R, including when it comes to seat (located 810 mm off the ground, 15 mm lower than on the base bike), handlebar, and footpeg triangle.
When it comes to the way it looks, the new sportsbike is heavily inspired by its sibling, but also throws in some specific design cues. There are LED lights all around, front air intakes to help it breathe and cool, a fresh cowl design, and a rounded profile for the entire front section.
Suzuki says it will make the new bike available to riders in the summer of next year, so there's plenty of waiting to do until the two-wheeler actually gets here. When it lands, it will be offered in three color schemes: Pearl Vigor Blue and Metallic Mystic Silver, Pearl Pulse Red and Solid Iron Grey, and Glass Sparkle Black and Metallic Galaxy Grey.
Seeing how the official launch of the model is more than half a year away, Suzuki makes no mention of how much it will charge for the GSX-10R. For the record, the GSX-R1000R presently goes for around $18,000.
